subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow read-tool safe fallback for binary document formats now, or defer this behavior to broader document parsing/provider-native file input work?
rationale: The source-proven problem is narrow, but parsing and provider-native forwarding overlap with security-sensitive and product-sensitive document-input designs that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Add Narrow Read Fallback
options.body: Detect common binary document types before text decoding and return an actionable message, using the existing `pdf` tool as the PDF parser path.

options.title: Defer To Document Input Design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader provider-native file/document and Office extraction boundaries are approved together.

options.title: Implement Core Parsing
options.body: Add in-core extraction for selected document formats, accepting the larger dependency and security-review surface.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Read Fallback
recommendation.body: Detect common binary document types before text decoding and return an actionable message, using the existing `pdf` tool as the PDF parser path.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current blame/history signal on the read-tool implementation and prior review context for this exact product-boundary decision.
